summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop subsystem using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, covering all 12 subcommands in a single tabbed interface with full CRUD management.
summary.outcome: A 4-tab bubbletea TUI (`entire memory-loop tui`) was implemented with Memories, Injection, History, and Settings tabs. The implementation is functional with orange accent colors, bordered detail panes, lifecycle actions, prompt testing, and settings cycling — though several visual polish iterations were required.

repo: The CLI uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256-color styling and respects `NO_COLOR` and `ACCESSIBLE=1` env vars.
The `memoryloop` package exposes `TransitionRecordLifecycle`, `SelectRelevant`, `AddManualRecord`, `PruneRecords`, and `SaveState` as the core mutation functions.
The project follows a package-per-feature structure: `memoryloop/`, `insights/`, `settings/` — the TUI was placed in `memorylooptui/` to match.
The `docs/superpowers/` directory is gitignored — brainstorming artifacts and specs written there are not tracked.
The project uses lipgloss v1 API for TUI styling.

code.finding: In bubbletea's type switch `switch msg := msg.(type)`, the inner typed `msg` is scoped to each case. Delegation code outside the switch must use the outer `msg` parameter (type `tea.Msg`), but type assertions on it still work correctly since the underlying value is preserved.
Lipgloss color `"8"` (dark gray) is effectively invisible on dark terminals. Use `"245"` (light gray) for visible borders and inactive tab labels.

Settings key handling required refactoring the `tea.Cmd` closure to capture the full `settingsChangedMsg` struct rather than pointer fields from local variables to avoid scope/state issues with async bubbletea message dispatch.

workflow: Subagent-driven development works well for incremental TUI feature builds — dispatching Tasks 1-3 together as a single agent (since they're tightly coupled foundational scaffold) was more efficient than separate dispatches.
The brainstorm visual companion server (localhost) is ephemeral and needs to be restarted when the session ends — it doesn't persist between sessions.
Using debug logging to a file (not stdout, which bubbletea owns) is the correct approach for debugging bubbletea key handling issues.
Setting `maxWidth` caps (e.g., 80 cols) causes layout problems on wider terminals — content should adapt to actual terminal width from `WindowSizeMsg`.
Lipgloss border width must be explicitly set relative to the available width (`width - 2`) to render correctly; without it borders may not appear.
The visual companion mockups and the actual TUI can diverge significantly in spacing/borders — mockups use HTML/CSS which renders differently from terminal box-drawing characters.

friction: Lipgloss border color `"8"` was invisible on dark terminals, causing multiple 'borders not showing' feedback cycles before switching to `"245"`.

Settings tab key handling appeared broken for several iterations — root cause was unclear and required adding file-based debug logging to diagnose; turned out to work after refactoring the cmd closure.
Injection tab content overflowed terminal height pushing the tab bar off-screen, requiring explicit row count caps on the log table.
The `maxWidth=80` initial cap caused narrow layout on wider terminals and needed to be removed.
The visual companion server shut down between sessions, requiring a restart and re-generation of all HTML mockup content.
open_items: History tab `R` key (trigger refresh) is a placeholder — async refresh via bubbletea spinner is not yet wired to the actual `memoryloop` refresh function.
No unit tests for the TUI package — the design spec explicitly deferred this to 'manual verification'.
The `prune` action keybinding (`D`) was added to the spec late but its full UX (confirmation dialog) may not be fully implemented.
Injection tab prompt tester match scoring display may need real integration testing with actual memory data.
The visual companion server needs a persistent restart mechanism or the mockup HTML should be committed somewhere accessible.
